<observation>
  <type>feature</type>
  <title>Added opt-in majority vote for observation extraction in ExtractionConsistency</title>
  <subtitle>New service implements majority vote logic for observation extraction, wired into AgentService.</subtitle>
  <facts>
    <fact>New file backend/src/main/java/com/ablueforce/cortexce/service/ExtractionConsistency.java implements majority vote for observation extraction.</fact>

A dedicated test class ExtractionConsistencyTest was also created to validate the new behavior. The change spans 4 files with 210 insertions and 11 deletions, indicating a substantial new capability.</narrative>

<observation>
  <type>change</type>
  <title>Removed non-security qualifier from Fixed verb definition in continuation.txt</title>
  <subtitle>Reverted prompt template wording that had narrowed the Fixed verb to non-security defects only.</subtitle>
  <facts>
    <fact>The phrase "in non-security code" was removed from the Fixed verb definition in backend/src/main/resources/prompts/continuation.txt.</fact>
    <fact>The Fixed verb line now reads "Fixed: a defect already produced wrong or failing behaviour." without a security-domain qualifier.</fact>
    <fact>The commit touched 2 files: backend/src/main/resources/prompts/continuation.txt and backend/src/main/resources/prompts/init.txt, with 10 insertions and 14 deletions.</fact>
    <fact>The commit message states the revert was motivated by a drop in type accuracy after the domain-first security verb change.</fact>
  </facts>
  <narrative>A prior change had scoped the "Fixed" verb in the prompt templates to "non-security code" in order to distinguish security bugfixes from regular ones. That narrowing caused type accuracy to drop, so the qualifier was reverted. The Fixed definition in continuation.txt now applies to any defect that already produced wrong or failing behaviour, regardless of security domain. The parallel init.txt prompt file was updated in the same commit, keeping the two prompt templates consistent.</narrative>
